transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-04
Time: 16:00 UTC / 11:00 ET
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Redwood CSM); Samir Patel (Helios Procurement), Laura Kim (Helios CISO), Raj Singh (Helios Head Eng), Nina Park (Helios Legal)

Summary (auto): Align on MSA/DPA markups, SLAs, and next steps for pilot and procurement approvals.

00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, yeah thanks for joining on short notice, um this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the account. With me is Diego our solutions engineer and Priya who will be your CSM if we move forward.
00:12 Samir Patel: Hey Maya, thanks - we got a pretty full deck from procurement side, so I appreciate you fitting us in.
00:18 Laura Kim: Hi all, Laura here. I'll be focused on security and compliance bits - I had a few follow-ups on the DPA and KMS notes.
00:25 Maya Chen: Great, thanks Laura. Nina from legal?
00:28 Nina Park: Yep hi, Nina - I'll be tracking the MSA redlines, payment terms, things like that.
00:33 Diego Alvarez: Quick intro on my side: I'll run through the SLA and what's practically achievable from an inference standpoint - latency/RTO stuff and how we handle fallbacks.
00:42 Raj Singh: And I'm Raj, engineering. We'll be doing the pilot and benchmarks, so I'll have technical questions around private deployment and VPC peering.
00:51 Maya Chen: Perfect. Agenda for today: 1) redline MSA/DPA items, 2) SLA expectations, 3) pricing/approval timeline, and 4) pilot scope/onboarding timing. Does that look right?
01:00 Samir Patel: Yep, thanks.
01:05 Nina Park: Good, let's start with the MSA. We flagged payment terms - we'd like net 30 rather than net 45 - and also a standard indemnification clause tweak.
01:18 Maya Chen: Understood. On payment terms we can discuss; our standard is 45 but enterprise deals can go to 30 with procurement approval. I'll note that as an action. For indemnity, can you send the exact language you want redlined?
01:33 Nina Park: I'll send a marked-up MSA after the call. Also around data residency - we need clarity on logs retention and audit access in a private deployment.
01:45 Priya Narang: That's great to capture - we have an onboarding checklist that maps to those items. For the private offering, logs can be kept per customer policy and we integrate with your KMS.
01:57 Laura Kim: On KMS - we require customer-managed keys for production PHI handling. Is that available in Redwood Private?
02:06 Diego Alvarez: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported on our Private deployments. We plug into your KMS/HSM and keys never leave your control. There are a couple of setup steps for rotations but it's standard.
02:20 Laura Kim: Ok, good. Also need SOC2 Type II and ISO attestations.
02:24 Priya Narang: We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs - I can put them in a secure link after the meeting.
02:30 Nina Park: Please do. Also for the DPA, we need stronger breach notification timelines - 48 hours preferred.
02:37 Maya Chen: Our DPA standard is 72 hours, but we can escalate that for enterprise contracts; I'll put that on the table.
02:44 Samir Patel: Great. Moving on to SLAs - we're targeting 99.9% availability for the inference endpoint with a clear credit schedule. Can Redwood commit to that?
02:55 Diego Alvarez: We offer SLA tiers; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can reach 99.9% with regional redundancy and committed capacity. For hosted, it's often 99.5 unless you purchase a higher tier. The credits structure is in Appendix A, but we can draft one that meets your needs.
03:13 Raj Singh: Latency targets are also important. We need p95 under 300 ms for our common prompt sizes (approx 512 tokens). Is that realistic?
03:22 Diego Alvarez: For Dedicated capacity yes, 300 ms p95 is achievable on our optimized GPU runtime depending on model and batch configuration. We'll need to baseline with your prompt load; that's what the pilot's for.
03:33 Raj Singh: Ok the pilot will include a synthetic traffic run and a replay of existing traffic.
03:39 Diego Alvarez: Exactly - we'll scope a two-week benchmark window where we run dedicated nodes and collect p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per token.
03:48 Maya Chen: For pricing - Samir, what's your approval path and timeline?
03:52 Samir Patel: We need procurement approval by Nov 15 to hit our Q4 budget window. We'll need a final pricing schedule and MSA by Nov 12 ideally.
04:03 Maya Chen: We can aim to get you a redlined MSA and pricing schedule by Nov 6, which should give legal and procurement time.
04:10 Nina Park: Can you include an example pricing calc for typical monthly volume - like 1M tokens / day estimate?
04:18 Maya Chen: Yes we'll include a proforma with estimated costs across hosted vs dedicated vs private. Also, note that Dedicated includes a reserved capacity discount and Private has a platform fee.
04:29 Samir Patel: Any flexibility on the platform fee for the first year?
04:32 Maya Chen: We can discuss a one-time onboarding credit or reduced platform fee as part of the commercial package. I'll put options in the schedule.
04:40 Laura Kim: Back to security - how do you handle audit logs and access? We need to ensure logs are immutable and there's an audit trail for admin actions.
04:48 Diego Alvarez: Audit logs are retained per customer policy; for Private, logs can be pushed to your SIEM. Admin actions are tracked and we support RBAC and SSO with SAML/IdP. We can provide sample schema for the logs.
05:01 Laura Kim: Good. Also, vulnerability scanning cadence and pen test results?
05:05 Priya Narang: We run quarterly scanning and annual third-party pen tests; results can be shared under NDA and we provide mitigation timelines in our security packet.
05:14 Nina Park: We'll want a statement on data deletion upon contract termination in the DPA.
05:19 Maya Chen: Standard clause is data deletion within 30 days of termination; we can shorten that if required.
05:25 Raj Singh: For the pilot, we plan to run on our VPC with peered networking and test with customer-managed KMS. Can you walk through the onboarding steps?
05:36 Diego Alvarez: Sure - step 1: account provisioning and RBAC; step 2: VPC peering and firewall rules; step 3: KMS integration; step 4: model pinning and rollout config; step 5: benchmark runs. We'll supply a runbook and a Terraform module to automate the peering.
05:54 Raj Singh: Terraform module - good. Which cloud regions do you support for Private?
05:58 Diego Alvarez: We support AWS regions in US-East, US-West, and EU-Central for Private deployments; on-prem is also possible with our on-prem appliance.
06:06 Raj Singh: On-prem would be a stretch for us; we'll try VPC peering first.
06:10 Maya Chen: Ok. Timeline recap: we'll send the redlined MSA, pricing, SOC2/ISO docs, and SLA appendix by Nov 6. Pilot kickoff proposed Nov 15, two-week benchmarking window through Nov 22.
06:24 Samir Patel: That timeline works but it depends on legal sign-off. If you can get docs on Nov 6, we'll prioritize review.
06:31 Maya Chen: Sounds good. Any competitor constraints or existing commitments?
06:35 Nina Park: We're also evaluating Anthropic for the model quality and OpenAI for latency, but those vendors have higher hosted costs; we're looking for the right mix of performance and security.
06:47 Maya Chen: Understood - we'll include a comparison sheet focused on throughput/cost/controls so you can share with stakeholders.
06:55 Raj Singh: A couple of technical clarifications - what's your policy around model weights? We need assurance that model weights are not swapped without notice in private deployments.
07:05 Diego Alvarez: For Private, model binaries are customer-managed; we only orchestrate. For Hosted we maintain model catalog and provide notices for major changes; model pinning is supported so you can lock versions.
07:18 Raj Singh: Good. Also, how do you handle KV cache persistence across restarts? We worry about cold starts affecting latency.
07:25 Diego Alvarez: For Dedicated we keep KV cache warm with continuous batching and optional pre-warming; for strict SLAs we recommend a small reserved pool to reduce cold starts.
07:36 Laura Kim: Anything special about PHI handling we should be aware of?
07:40 Maya Chen: We'll treat PHI as sensitive data - Private plus customer KMS and audit trails is the recommended path. We'll also sign BAAs as needed; I'll confirm.
07:49 Nina Park: Please send the redline process and confirm BAAs are supported.
07:53 Priya Narang: Yes, BAAs supported - we'll include a draft.
07:57 Samir Patel: On procurement approvals - who should I expect to receive the invoice and PO details from?
08:02 Maya Chen: Invoices will be sent from Redwood Billing; I'll include the billing contact in the email and cc Priya for onboarding.
08:09 Samir Patel: Okay.
08:12 Maya Chen: Any other blockers?
08:15 Laura Kim: Just to reiterate: 48-hour breach notice preferred, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 docs, and data deletion window confirmed.
08:26 Maya Chen: We'll list those as required items and put proposed compromises in the MSA redline.
08:32 Nina Park: One more on indemnity - we'll send the preferred language but open to discussion.
08:38 Maya Chen: Great.
08:40 Maya Chen: Quick recap of action items: Maya will send redlined MSA and pricing by Nov 6; Priya share SOC2 and ISO by Nov 5; Diego prepare pilot runbook/Terraform and benchmark plan by Nov 10; Samir to confirm procurement timeline by Nov 12. Anything to add?
08:58 Samir Patel: That covers it.
09:00 Raj Singh: We'll prepare test datasets and access for the pilot; Diego, we'll coordinate on the replay data formatting.
09:06 Diego Alvarez: I'll send sample schema and ingestion steps today.
09:10 Maya Chen: Ok last thing - scheduling: does Nov 15 for kickoff work for everyone?
09:14 Samir Patel: Tentatively yes, pending docs.
09:16 Maya Chen: Great - we'll follow up with calendar invite once docs are out. Thanks everyone.
09:21 Laura Kim: Thanks all.
09:23 Nina Park: Thanks.
09:25 End of recording.

References to Redwood product names: Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private, Redwood Console (may appear as 'Redwood influence' in some lines).
